reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin mining packages and urges viewers to recruit new miners as a way to increase the coin's market price. It presents collective recruitment as the mechanism for creating value, telling the network to bring packages into the business and build networks rather than merely reporting on or criticizing the offer. The promotional framing is reinforced by repeated OneCoin and Forbes imagery.

citations.quote: The more people who start mining the one coin The higher the price of the coin in the market
We do that by attracting new miners into the business
make sure to really bring the packages inside the business
start building your networks properly educate your people

opening.argument: Judge the video by the question it puts to viewers: “Which is fake? You decide!” That framing invites scrutiny of the OneCoin and Forbes relationship rather than asking viewers to accept it as settled. The speaker also says the company will not raise the coin’s value for participants; the stated theory depends on what the network does. Neither statement verifies the mining or price claims. In a video that openly raises authenticity, the promotional speech can be heard as material for viewers to examine, not a claim the video has proved.

citations.quote: Onecoin - Forbes - Which is fake? You decide!
the company will not do it for us we are the network

rebuttal.rebuttal: The quoted recruitment instructions are real, but they do not settle how the video presents that speech. “We do that by attracting new miners” identifies what the speaker wants; it does not answer the title’s explicit authenticity question. The prosecution treats the displayed pitch as the video’s own endorsement without resolving that framing.

citations.quote: We do that by attracting new miners into the business
Which is fake? You decide!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title poses a question, but the recorded speech does not warn viewers away from the offer or test its claims. It directly tells them to bring packages into the business and concludes by urging them to come in and mine coins. Saying the company will not do it for them shifts the work to participants; it does not retract the recruitment pitch.

citations.quote: make sure to really bring the packages inside the business
It means, come in, mine your coins and that's it.

opening.argument: This can be read as a demonstration of how a network pitch works. The speaker explains a proposed connection between participation and coin price, then tells existing participants to “start building your networks properly” and “educate your people.” The video also shows a Forbes-branded magazine being handled, while its title asks viewers to decide what is fake. Those elements give a careful viewer material to evaluate: a claim about value, a recruitment method, and a magazine association. Showing and explaining that method is not, by itself, proof that a viewer is being offered a verified return.

citations.quote: The more people who start mining the one coin The higher the price of the coin in the market
start building your networks properly educate your people
Onecoin - Forbes - Which is fake? You decide!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes the speaker’s instructions, but instructions can also be the subject of a demonstration. The magazine imagery and the title’s question leave open whether the video is asking viewers to inspect the pitch and its claimed association with Forbes. The quoted price assertion does not independently establish that the price responds as claimed.

citations.quote: Onecoin - Forbes - Which is fake? You decide!
The more people who start mining the one coin The higher the price of the coin in the market

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demonstration would need some separation between explaining a pitch and urging participation. Here the speaker addresses the network as “we,” tells it to attract new miners, and calls for packages to be brought into the business. The magazine pages do not change the direct call to act, and the price claim need not be true for the solicitation to be promotional.

citations.quote: We do that by attracting new miners into the business
make sure to really bring the packages inside the business

opening.argument: The speech describes a business network recruiting participants, but the supplied words do not specify a payment amount, a guaranteed return, or a reward for each recruit. “Packages” are mentioned without their terms. The speaker’s claim about a higher coin price is a claim about market value, not a quoted promise to pay each viewer. A judge can recognize ordinary business promotion and an unverified price theory here without treating the missing financial terms as established facts.

citations.quote: We do that by attracting new miners into the business
make sure to really bring the packages inside the business
The more people who start mining the one coin The higher the price of the coin in the market

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s quotes establish recruitment and mention packages, but “bring the packages inside the business” gives no price or purchase terms. Nor does the quoted appeal to build networks say that participants receive downline payments. The speech may be promotional, but those excerpts alone leave the transaction and compensation mechanism unspecified.

citations.quote: make sure to really bring the packages inside the business
start building your networks properly educate your people

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a price list or guaranteed payout does not turn this into ordinary commerce. The speaker links more miners to a higher coin price, says the network can push that value up, identifies attracting new miners as the way to do it, and urges participants to bring packages into the business. The proposed benefit and recruitment mechanism are explicit even though package terms are not.

we want to push this coin as high up as we can
